warning: Optional methods, not current evidence or evaluation references.

examples.description: Compare a defined demand window with modeled stock.
examples.method: Delegate qualifying units and calendar-day boundaries to retail, then modeled stock at the cutoff to inventory. Use local result SQL for the ratio; zero demand is undefined.
examples.illustrative_answer: If recorded stock is 12 units and 6 qualifying units sold over 30 calendar days, the illustrative coverage is 60 days under constant demand. This is not a forecast or physical availability guarantee.

examples.description: Reconcile stock across centers including unknown attribution.
examples.method: Ask distribution for inventory-item center groups, preserving null and unmatched center IDs. Compare their sum with inventory's same-scope total.
examples.illustrative_answer: A demonstration split of 4, 3 and 2 unknown units reconciles to 9 total units. Unknown attribution is a data gap, not a new physical facility.

examples.description: Prioritize products using observed demand and stock.
examples.method: Ask retail for product-level qualifying units and inventory for product-level modeled stock. Join by product ID, not product name. Define any prioritization rule explicitly.
examples.illustrative_answer: An illustrative product with 2 units and a measured rate of 0.5 units per day has 4 modeled days of coverage; replenishment priority still depends on lead time and service policy.

examples.description: Assess possible transfer routes without executing transfers.
examples.method: Ask distribution to obtain current Maps routes only if configured, while keeping source/destination stock evidence separate. Require actual capacity and authorization before any operational claim.
examples.illustrative_answer: A returned driving duration could support a routing comparison; it cannot confirm truck clearance, carrier pricing, warehouse capacity or delivery.

examples.description: Reject incompatible metrics and population joins.
examples.method: Check scope, grain, snapshot and time before combining specialist artifacts. Ask for a corrected aggregate if definitions differ.
examples.illustrative_answer: A revenue ranking cannot establish demand units or stock coverage. Distinct customers per category cannot be summed into a brand total without overlap accounting.

examples.description: Use previous scoped evidence for a follow-up.
examples.method: Read exact prior evidence or delegate a focused clarification when the question changes the period, cohort or denominator. Do not automatically repeat every specialist call.
examples.illustrative_answer: A follow-up asking for a concise interpretation can reuse unchanged counts, while a different business cutoff requires new stock evidence.

examples.description: Separate observed changes from causal hypotheses.
examples.method: Combine actual sales and inventory observations only at matching scope and dates. State missing stockout history, demand and operational data explicitly.
examples.illustrative_answer: Lower recorded stock and falling sales may coexist; those observations alone do not prove that stockouts caused the sales decline.

examples.description: Save a combined report only on the user's explicit request.
examples.method: Finish the cross-domain analysis and stage only an authorized report save. Use the actual operation receipt and do not claim stock movements or purchases.
examples.illustrative_answer: The application can save a reviewed report. It cannot dispatch inventory, place a purchase order or promise that a proposed transfer occurred.
